newsitem.title: EGYPT: Christopher says Arabs, Israelis committed to peace.
newsitem.headline: Christopher says Arabs, Israelis committed to peace.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Tuesday Arabs and Israelis remained committed to forging ahead with the peace process despite the "traumas" that had hit the Middle East in the past year.
Christopher told a Middle East and North African economic conference that for future negotiations to succeed, each side must recognise there could be no winners or losers.
Christopher said he believed an agreement in current Israeli-Palestinian talks on an Israeli troop deployment in the West Bank town of Hebron was "close at hand".
Robert Pelletreau, a U.S. assistant secretary of state for the region, said both sides were close to agreeing on zones in Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Arabs.
"They are close to agreement on the different points that they have been negotiating in the last three weeks, about the points about the different zones," he told Reuters.

"They are at a point now where if they wanted to, they could reach agreement in 24 hours more. But it could also take two or three weeks," Pelletreau said. "It's a question of how much you are going to tie the Hebron agreement with non-Hebron issues and that still hasn't been resolved."

Officials say among the main elements Arafat is seeking are further Israeli redeployments from the rest of the West Bank -- which had been due to start last September -- a date for resuming final status talks and cessation of settlement activites.

Christopher's spokesman Nicholas Burns advised journalists against expecting a deal in the next few days. He said a 90- minute meeting between Christopher and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had not shown "any specific progress" on Hebron.

In what is likely to be his last major speech on the Middle East, Christopher, who will step down in January, said there was "no doubt that the peace process has been tested -- tested severely -- by the traumas of the last year".

He was apparently referring to the assassination of Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin a year ago, a string of suicide bombings in Israel by Moslem militants in February and March, and bloody Israeli-Palestinian clashes in September.
"But over the past year, and especially in recent weeks, the peace process has also demonstrated great resilience," the secretary of state said.

"Arabs and Israelis alike know what war means. They have already glimpsed the promise of peace. By looking back into the abyss, both Arabs and Israelis recognised the imperative of moving forward," he said.
Once the Hebron talks finally succeeded, Christopher said he expected the parties to "move ahead with the same sense of urgency to implement the remainder of (their) Interim Agreement".
Israel and the Palestinians have scheduled negotiations due to end by 1999 on the final status of the Palestinian self-rule areas in the West Bank and Gaza, and on Jerusalem.

Christopher pledged that U.S. President Bill Clinton, re- elected last week, and the next secretary of state, who has not yet been named, would continue to make Middle East peace a top priority over the next four years.
